newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber offer prices were generally stable in late trading on Friday amid thin volumes, traders said.

They said a deal was done in the afternoon at 46.50 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for August shipment and at 47.25 fob Medan. Offer prices were quoted at 46.50 fob Padang and Surabaya and at 46.50 fob Pontianak and Jambi.

"The market is generally stable and demand is still thin. We expect prices to stay the same next week because the market lacks fresh factors which can change the price trend, either upward or downward," said one trader.
Traders said news about a plan by the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) to resume market intervention in order to stabilise prices did not have much impact.
"I personally believe that INRO is not effective at all. It's only beneficial for the consumers and not the producers. That's why many traders are taking the news for granted," said another trader.
Traders said supply was tight in the local market because there were not many tappers around.

"Tappers have felt that it's better for them to find other jobs elsewhere because of the poor rubber prices. They think the daily wage they obtain through tapping is not enough to support their lives," said one trader.
Some traders said many rubber collectors who employed the tappers were also hoarding stocks, waiting for better prices.
